issues_detected.description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false, but the record's own cohort definitions enroll participants with Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, mild cognitive impairment, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, active manic or depressive episodes, and alcohol or substance use disorder. These are populations conventionally treated as vulnerable under human-subjects regulation, primarily because of consent capacity. The false value is partly reconciled by special_protections, which restricts the adult cohort to participants able to provide informed consent for themselves in English, but the flag as written understates the population the dataset covers.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set at_risk_groups_included to true and use special_protections to state the capacity-to-consent screen, or add a source_caveat explaining that the false value follows a source statement rather than the cohort composition.

issues_detected.description: data_protection_impacts is populated with an ethics review of sensitive fields and a published controlled-access memorandum, while its own source_caveats records that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether an impact analysis on data subjects was conducted. The slot therefore reads as a completed impact assessment when the source denies one was performed. The record discloses the tension rather than concealing it, which limits the severity.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the caveat and lead the impact_details with the source's own negative answer, so the slot is not read as an affirmative DPIA.

issues_detected.description: The citation carries RRID:SCR_007345, which is the Research Resource Identifier for PhysioNet, the hosting repository, not for the Bridge2AI-Voice dataset. The format is valid and the placement follows the PhysioNet citation convention, but a reader may take it as a dataset-level RRID.
issues_detected.recommendation: Note in the citation or in notes that the RRID identifies the PhysioNet platform rather than this dataset.

issues_detected.description: file_collections and distribution_formats describe every table as paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name, yet the variables slot is empty. The record documents that variable-level metadata exists without carrying any of it, so no column name, type, or permissible value is machine-readable from the datasheet.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate variables for at least the demographics, diagnosis and enrollment tables, or state in notes that variable-level documentation is deferred to the released JSON dictionaries.

issues_detected.description: No size metadata is carried anywhere in the record. total_size_bytes and total_file_count are absent and no file_collection reports total_bytes, so a prospective user cannot estimate the download or storage cost of nine Parquet feature files before requesting credentialed access. Instance counts and per-feature record counts are present and carry the question, but they only permit an estimate.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add total_size_bytes or per-collection total_bytes from the PhysioNet file listing.

issues_detected.description: conforms_to carries the free-text label 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0' rather than a resolvable identifier for the standard. The value is unambiguous to a human reader and conforms_to_standard separately carries the token BIDS, so machine resolution is partly recoverable, but the slot is not a dereferenceable reference.
issues_detected.recommendation: Use the BIDS specification URI alongside the version label.

issues_detected.description: keywords carries four terms (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai). None names the modality (speech, audio, respiratory sounds), the disease areas the dataset is organized around (voice disorders, Parkinson's disease, dementia, depression, chronic cough), the data types released (Parquet, spectrogram, MFCC), or the intended application (machine learning, digital biomarker). Discoverability is materially below what the record's own description supports.
issues_detected.recommendation: Expand to at least eight keywords drawn from the cohort names, the acoustic feature types and the AI/ML application framing already present in the description.

semantic_insights: DOI prefix 10.13026 is PhysioNet and is used correctly; the version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, the page URL .../b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ and version 3.1.0 agree with one another, and version_access separately carries the version-independent DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42.

All four award identifiers follow NIH form: OT2OD032720 is a valid activity-code-plus-institute-plus-serial core number for the Common Fund Other Transaction mechanism, and 1OT2OD032720-01, 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and 3OT2OD032720-01S3 are well-formed application, supplement and amendment renderings of it. The record records each as its source states it rather than normalizing, and funders.notes explicitly identifies two further strings in the documentation as corrupted renderings of the same award.

HIPAA Safe Harbor is the appropriate deidentification standard for this data type, and the record goes beyond it correctly: it removes indirect identifiers, generalizes geography to country, strips narrative text and free-speech transcripts, and withholds raw waveforms entirely because voice is inherently identifying. participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states the residual risk in the same terms and discloses that k-anonymity with k of two or more is not achieved, which is an unusually candid negative finding.

The human-subjects consistency chain holds end to end: involves_human_subjects true leads to ethical_reviews naming the USF single IRB and the separate Canadian research ethics boards, to informed_consent with documented consent modes and a withdrawal mechanism, to consent_revocations stating the point past which withdrawal cannot remove data, and to participant_compensation with per-session amounts and a stated cap.

Access tiering is internally coherent across four slots: distribution_formats routes Parquet and TSV to the PhysioNet URL and WAV to Synapse; license_and_use_terms names the registered-access license; data_governance.access_review_process gives the credentialing path for each tier; and third_party_sharing states the sharing model. A reader can reconstruct the full access path for either tier without leaving the record.

Temporal ordering is sound: project start September 2022, twelve months of collection, releases running November 2024 through May 2026, and issued 2026-05-01 matching the v3.1.0 release date in distribution_dates.

The record separates sensitive_elements (present, true) from confidential_elements (present, false) correctly. Confidentiality is scoped to legal privilege and doctor-patient communication, not to health sensitivity, so the two values are not in conflict despite regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level being restricted.

known_biases uses five distinct enum-shaped categories (selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) rather than free prose, and the measurement_bias entry identifies a real confound the source documents support: cohort membership is entangled with recording site and with the specific tablet device used there.

source_caveats is used throughout as a disagreement register rather than as filler. It records the Health Data Nexus versus MIT hosting discrepancy, the 10,000 versus 30,000 enrollment target conflict, the 61,937 recording count that the preferred source does not carry, and the FFT parameter change between v1.1 and v3.1.0, each with the reason one source was preferred.

Provenance is traceable as a chain rather than as a version list: raw WAV entities, a named standardization and feature-extraction activity with concrete parameters (monaural, 16 kHz, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, 50 Hz articulatory sampling), the b2aiprep 3.0.0 agent, and a typed derives_from relation to the controlled-access Synapse deposit.

questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated
questions.score_label: Approximately 79% fields populated
questions.evidence: Present (11 of 14): id doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description ~2,000 characters; keywords 4 terms; license_and_use_terms with data_use_permission general_research_use; doi 10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; creators 18 entries with affiliations; purposes 3 entries; instances 2 entries with counts 833; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level restricted. Absent (3 of 14): resources, parent_datasets, variables.
questions.quality_note: Eleven of the fourteen named fields are populated with substantive content, not placeholders. The three gaps are real: variables is empty although file_collections describes a JSON data dictionary for every released table, and parent_datasets is empty although the derivation from the controlled-access raw audio is stated in related_datasets under derives_from. Falls between the 70% and 90% bands, closer to the upper.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields have meaningful content length
questions.score_label: Greater than 200 characters
questions.evidence: description spans lines 46-75, approximately 2,000 characters across two paragraphs, naming 833 participants, five North American sites, four adult disease cohorts, seventeen acoustic tasks by name and twelve validated questionnaires by acronym. purposes carries three responses totalling approximately 750 characters. Mean well above 200.
questions.quality_note: Length here is carrying information density rather than padding. The description alone specifies the cohort structure, the task protocol, the diagnostic gold standards, the released file formats and the raw-audio withholding decision.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords describing topic coverage
questions.score_label: 3 to 7 keywords
questions.evidence: keywords: voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai. Four unique terms.
questions.quality_note: The weakest structural element of the record. Four terms for a dataset whose own description names four disease cohorts, seventeen acoustic tasks, nine derived feature families and two distribution formats. Nothing in the keyword list would surface this record for a search on speech, dementia, Parkinson's, depression, chronic cough, spectrogram, MFCC or machine learning, all of which the record documents at length elsewhere. Semantic note: the terms present are accurate, so this is a coverage gap rather than a correctness problem.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of distribution formats and file type diversity
questions.score_label: More than 3 file types
questions.evidence: Four distinct types: Apache Parquet (nine named files: ppgs, sparc_ema, sparc_loudness, sparc_periodicity, sparc_pitch, torchaudio_spectrogram, torchaudio_mfcc, torchaudio_pitch, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram), tab-separated values (audio_quality_metrics.tsv, static_features.tsv, phenotype tables), JSON data dictionaries paired with every table, and WAV audio under controlled access. file_collections enumerates four collections with paths, collection_type values and per-folder file listings; total_file_count is absent.
questions.quality_note: Enumeration is at the individual-file level for the features collection and at the subfolder level for phenotype, listing eighteen diagnosis tables and thirteen questionnaire tables by name. The variety is genuine multi-modal structure, matching the description's account of dense derived features alongside tabular phenotype data, not format padding.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or instance count metadata
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: instances[0].counts: 833. instances[1].notes gives per-feature record counts: torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc electromagnetic articulography 28,640. version_access.version_details adds 12,523 recordings for 306 participants at initial release. subsets carries eight entries with is_subpopulation and is_data_split flags; splits states no recommended splits are provided.
questions.quality_note: Passes on instance counts, which are given at both participant and per-feature record level with an explanation of why the counts differ. No byte-level metadata anywhere: total_size_bytes, total_file_count and file_collections.total_bytes are all absent, so the counts support only an estimate of download size.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 with id as the matching CURIE doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66; page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; publisher https://physionet.org; RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation; version_access.latest_version_doi doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42.
questions.quality_note: Passes with more than one persistent identifier. The 10.13026 prefix is the PhysioNet registrant and is used correctly. Both a version-pinned DOI and a version-independent DOI are carried, which is the correct pattern for a dataset on its sixth release.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, creator affiliations, and institutional sponsors
questions.score_label: Funders with grants plus creators with affiliations
questions.evidence: funders.grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, through the Bridge2AI program' with four grant entries: OT2OD032720 with project title, awardee institution, principal investigator and the dates 1 September 2022 to 30 November 2026; 3OT2OD032720-01S1; 1OT2OD032720-01; and 3OT2OD032720-01S3 with NIH RePORTER application ID 11376382, fiscal year 2025 and an award amount of 4,660,942 US dollars. creators lists 18 entries, 17 named, each with a named affiliation carrying department, institution, city and country.
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive on both halves of the criterion. Award numbers are well-formed NIH identifiers and the record does not silently normalize the variants across sources; funders.notes goes further and identifies two malformed strings in the documentation as corrupted renderings of the same award. Twelve creators also carry CRediT-style credit_roles, and where a role assignment is inferred rather than stated the entry says so in its own source_caveats.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.applicability_evidence: description (Q1/Q2 field) states data were collected from '833 adult participants collected at five sites in North America' recruited 'at high-volume expert clinics'; collection_mechanisms (Q12 field) describes a tablet application 'presenting the acoustic tasks, demographic surveys, confounder questions and validated questionnaires' administered to participants. Human participants and clinical research are both evidenced outside Q8's own fields.
questions.description: Comprehensive ethics coverage across IRB, deidentification, privacy, consent, compensation and vulnerable populations
questions.score_label: Comprehensive human subjects protections and data protection impacts documented
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews carries two reviewing organizations, the USF single IRB and the Canadian research ethics boards at Mount Sinai, SickKids and the University of Toronto, with the reason the Canadian sites applied separately. human_subject_research gives irb_approval, ethics_review_board, regulatory_compliance including the partial HIPAA waiver for chart review and a Certificate of Confidentiality, and special_populations. is_deidentified gives method (HIPAA Safe Harbor plus indirect identifier removal), an itemized identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details stating that k-anonymity with k of two or more is not achieved. participant_privacy gives anonymization_method, privacy_techniques including federated learning, data_linkage and reidentification_risk. informed_consent gives consent_type, four documentation modes, consent_scope and withdrawal_mechanism. participant_compensation gives 40 or 80 US dollars per session with a 120 dollar cap. at_risk_populations and data_protection_impacts are populated. regulatory_restrictions gives hipaa_compliant compliant and other_compliance. data_governance names the Data Access Compliance Office with a contact address.
questions.quality_note: Every protection area named in the question is populated with specific, actionable content rather than assurance language, and several entries record negative findings that weaken the dataset's own position, including the failure to achieve k-anonymity and the healthsheet's 'No' answer on impact analysis. Semantic deduction considered and not applied: at_risk_groups_included is false while the cohorts include dementia and psychiatric populations, which is recorded as a medium consistency issue, but special_protections states the capacity-to-consent screen that substantively answers the concern, and the surrounding coverage is otherwise complete. The governance contact sits in data_governance rather than in regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact.

questions.name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions and confidentiality level are clearly defined
questions.score_label: License plus restrictions plus confidentiality classification
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission general_research_use with license_terms naming the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, the credentialing requirement, the duplication permission, the prohibition on sale and the Fort Lauderdale Agreement commitment. ip_restrictions carries four distinct restrictions covering copyright, the bar on IP claims that would block access, the downstream-rights carve-out and the absence of third-party restrictions. regulatory_restrictions gives confidentiality_level restricted, hipaa_compliant compliant, and other_compliance covering the Certificate of Confidentiality, the safeguards obligation, the five-business-day breach notification and the PhysioNet requirements. data_governance gives committee_name, accountable_organization, a tiered access_review_process and four stewardship_roles. retention_limit distinguishes indefinite hosting, two years for recipients and ten years for identifiable data held locally.
questions.quality_note: All three components of the top band are present and the governance content goes beyond them. The access process is documented separately for each tier and is specific enough to follow: PhysioNet credentialing plus a signed agreement for features, a Data Access Request Form and institutionally signed Data Use and Transfer Agreement routed through DACO for raw audio. Stewardship is allocated to named parties on both the provider and recipient side.

questions.name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
questions.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats is populated with three formats each carrying access_urls (PhysioNet and Synapse), and license_and_use_terms permits general_research_use by credentialed users. The datasets-shared condition is met.
questions.description: Standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance, typed cross-platform linkages and integration capability
questions.score_label: Standard formats plus schema/ontology compliance plus integration capability
questions.evidence: conforms_to 'Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0' with conforms_to_standard BIDS; conforms_to_schema https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema and conforms_to_class Dataset. Formats are Apache Parquet, TSV and WAV, all open. instances carry ontology CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:41, B2AI_TOPIC:4, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30 and B2AI_TOPIC:36; label_description references ICD-10 coding. related_datasets carries six typed relations (derives_from, is_supplemented_by, three is_new_version_of, is_version_of), each with a resolvable target across PhysioNet, Synapse and Health Data Nexus. external_resources links b2aiprep, senselab, the REDCap data dictionary and the documentation site, three of them with Zenodo archival DOIs. participant_privacy.data_linkage and instances[1].label_description name participant_id and session_id as the cross-table join keys.
questions.quality_note: Strong on every component the question names. The integration capability is concrete rather than asserted: named join keys usable across the feature and phenotype tables, per-file JSON data dictionaries keyed by column name, BIDS organization for the controlled-access audio, and ICD-10 diagnostic coding. Cross-platform linkage is typed rather than a bare URL list, which is what distinguishes this from a format-only record. Minor semantic note carried as a low-severity issue: conforms_to is a free-text label rather than a resolvable specification URI.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: external_resources (Q14 field) references two code repositories as dataset outputs: b2aiprep at https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep under Apache-2.0 and senselab at https://github.com/sensein/senselab, plus the REDCap data dictionary repository at https://github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap archived on Zenodo. purposes (Q7 field) also names creating 'new bioinformatics standards for acoustic and voice data collection, interoperability and analysis' as a project output. Condition met on fields outside Q11.
questions.description: Preprocessing, cleaning and labeling strategies with the software tools used
questions.score_label: Comprehensive strategies with software versions/URLs
questions.evidence: preprocessing_strategies carries six entries with concrete parameters: monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter; short-time FFT with a 25 ms window, 10 ms hop and 400-point FFT, spectrograms downsampled by two in time, 60 Mel bins and 60 MFCCs; Speech Articulatory Coding at 50 Hz over six vocal tract articulators, torchaudio pitch over 80 to 500 Hz and sparc pitch over 50 to 550 Hz; openSMILE, Parselmouth and Praat feature extraction with phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories at 100 Hz; HIPAA Safe Harbor deidentification; and BIDS conversion assembled with b2aiprep version 3.0.0. cleaning_strategies states that no cleaning preprocessing was applied and describes the audit protocol instead. labeling_strategies gives annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_platform REDCap, data_annotation_protocol and an inter_annotator_agreement statement. machine_annotation_tools lists nine tools with tool_descriptions and a tool_accuracy caveat. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and a no-imputation handling_strategy.
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive across every strategy slot the question names. Reproducibility rests on signal-processing parameters rather than on version pins, and those parameters are given at a level a reader could re-implement from. Version coverage is uneven, with b2aiprep pinned at 3.0.0 and Whisper identified as Large but openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, ppgs and senselab unversioned; repository URLs for the two central libraries are carried in external_resources rather than inline. The source_caveats on the FFT entry, recording that v1.1 used a 512-point FFT without time downsampling, is the kind of version-sensitive detail that makes the parameters usable. imputation_protocols is empty, correctly, because the record states no imputation was performed.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.applicability_evidence: Collection fields are populated (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors and collection_timeframes are all present) and the datasets-shared condition is met via distribution_formats with PhysioNet access_urls and a license permitting general research use.
questions.description: Completeness of collection mechanisms, acquisition methods, collectors and timeframes
questions.score_label: Full collection protocol with methods, collectors and timeframes
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods carries four typed entries with the schema booleans was_directly_observed, was_reported_by_subjects, was_validated_verified and was_inferred_derived, each with its own acquisition_details. collection_mechanisms names the custom tablet application, the specific hardware (iPad 9th or 10th generation and iPad Air 5th generation with an Avid AE-36 microphone through an Apple dongle, distinct devices per site) and the REDCap instruments. data_collectors carries two roles, researcher and academic_institution, describing the student and research-assistant staffing, the co-investigator listing of diagnosing clinicians and the five North American academic sites. collection_timeframes states twelve months. raw_data_sources carries three sources with source_type, raw_data_format and access_details including the Synapse accession syn72370534. sampling_strategies adds the recruitment rule, defining a high-volume expert clinic as one seeing more than 50 patients per month in the disease category.
questions.quality_note: All four components of the top band are present and the protocol is specific enough to reproduce, down to the microphone model and the clinic-volume threshold used for site selection. The timeframe is a duration without calendar anchors, which is a real limitation, but its source_caveats states that the healthsheet gives duration and no start or end dates, so the gap is attributed rather than glossed. Consent, notification and revocation are documented alongside in their own slots.

questions.name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
questions.applicability_evidence: Collection fields are populated (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors, collection_timeframes) and the datasets-shared condition is met via distribution_formats with PhysioNet access_urls.
questions.description: Version information, access methods, errata, update plans and data sustainability indicators
questions.score_label: Comprehensive versioning plus full sustainability documentation
questions.evidence: version 3.1.0. version_access lists six releases from 1.0 through 3.1.0 with dates and per-version DOIs, gives latest_version_doi doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 and states in version_details that older versions remain supported except v1.1, whose files are withdrawn. errata carries three entries: the v2.0 spectrogram reprocessing and free-speech feature removal, the v2.0.1 authorship correction and the v3.1.0 parquet repair. updates gives a semi-annual frequency, a changelog-based communication route and an itemized account of what v3.1.0 changed. maintainers carries three roles: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology for hosting, the consortium through DACO for curation and access, and NIH as the funding sponsor. publisher is PhysioNet, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository. retention_limit and extension_mechanism are populated.
questions.quality_note: All four sustainability indicators the question names are present: persistent identifiers at both version and concept level, a governance plan in data_governance and retention_limit, a domain-appropriate repository in PhysioNet, and institutional commitment through named MIT hosting and NIH funding. Version history is unusually complete for a sixth release, with a per-version DOI and a stated erratum for each correction. The maintainers entry carries a source_caveats resolving the Health Data Nexus versus MIT hosting discrepancy across sources rather than silently picking one.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.applicability_evidence: citation carries a formal dataset citation and external_resources carries the Interspeech 2024 protocol publication with its ISCA archive URL; the datasets-shared condition is met via distribution_formats with PhysioNet access_urls.
questions.description: Formal citations or external resources with DOI-linked references
questions.score_label: Multiple references and dataset citation
questions.evidence: citation gives a full formal dataset citation with twenty named authors, title, version, publisher, RRID:SCR_007345 and the resolving DOI https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66. external_resources carries seven entries including the Interspeech 2024 protocol development paper at its ISCA archive URL, two Zenodo archival DOIs (10.5281/zenodo.12760724 for the REDCap dictionary and 10.5281/zenodo.13834653 for the documentation site), two GitHub repositories with license terms, the FHIR voice biomarker profiles and the Voice Scholars training program. related_datasets adds five further DOIs across PhysioNet and Health Data Nexus. notes references the consortium's published AI-readiness self-assessment.
questions.quality_note: Both halves of the top band are met: a properly formed dataset citation and multiple external references, most DOI-linked. The record distinguishes archival from non-archival resources with the archival boolean and records that the healthsheet answered 'NA' to persistence guarantees for external resources, which is the honest reading rather than an assumed guarantee. Named publications by title are limited to the Interspeech protocol paper; the feasibility publication and the audiomics white paper are referenced repeatedly in caveats without their own citation entries.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.applicability_evidence: description (Q1/Q2 field) states 833 adult participants recruited at five North American sites in four disease cohorts; collection_mechanisms (Q12 field) describes demographic surveys and validated questionnaires administered to participants. Human participants and clinical research are evidenced outside Q15's own fields.
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity and subgroup details
questions.score_label: Detailed subgroup criteria with qualitative demographic characterization
questions.evidence: instances gives counts 833 with a participant instance_type and a label_description covering diagnostic labelling. subsets carries five population cohorts, each with inclusion and exclusion criteria at clinical specificity, for instance the neurological cohort 'aged over 44 and under 85, able to read and speak English' with named diagnoses and validation by brain CT, MRI, whole genome sequencing and serum p-tau. subpopulations gives identification by 'age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status in the demographics instrument' and a distribution statement that cohorts are not equally represented and that skews exist by disorder, site and demographic factors. at_risk_populations gives the 18-and-over eligibility and English-language requirement. missing_data_documentation explains that cohort-specific instruments are systematically absent outside their cohort.
questions.quality_note: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are as detailed as any clinical protocol, cohort by cohort, with the diagnostic gold standard named for each. What is missing is the demographic half: no counts or proportions by age, sex, gender, race, ethnicity or site appear anywhere in the record, so a reader learns which demographic variables were collected and that the distribution is skewed, but not how. For a dataset whose stated purpose is a demographically diverse resource and whose known_biases centre on representation, the absence of any numeric breakdown is a substantive gap. Scored one band below the top on that basis.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation
questions.score_label: Pass
questions.evidence: page https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/; publisher https://physionet.org; doi 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 with version-independent doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42; distribution_formats.access_urls to PhysioNet and https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/; external_resources to github.com/sensein/b2aiprep, github.com/sensein/senselab, github.com/eipm/bridge2ai-redcap, two Zenodo DOIs, https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, the ISCA archive and https://www.b2aivoicescholars.org/.
questions.quality_note: Passes comfortably. Persistent identifiers exist at three levels: the version DOI, the concept DOI resolving to the latest version, and archival Zenodo DOIs for the supporting code and documentation. All domains are plausible and consistent with the platforms the record names elsewhere.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats is populated with three formats each carrying access_urls, and license_and_use_terms permits general_research_use. The datasets-shared condition is met.
questions.description: How users can obtain the dataset
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path
questions.evidence: data_governance.access_review_process gives both tiers step by step: for features, register on PhysioNet, confirm identity, become a credentialed user and sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement, with no additional training required; for raw audio, complete a Data Access Request Form and Data Use Agreement, submit to DACO@b2ai-voice.org, and on approval have an authorized institutional official sign a Data Use and Transfer Agreement before release through Synapse. distribution_formats routes each format to its platform URL. license_and_use_terms names the license and states that no fees apply. third_party_sharing.is_shared true describes the registered and credentialed access model. raw_data_sources.access_details repeats the controlled-access route with the Synapse accession.
questions.quality_note: Platform, credentialing requirement, agreement and reviewing body are all named for each tier, and the record is explicit that no fee applies. A prospective user can determine which tier holds the data they need and what they must do to obtain it without consulting another document. No download_url slot is populated, but access_urls carry the equivalent and a bare download link would misrepresent a credentialed-access dataset.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License clarity with intended, prohibited and discouraged uses plus social impact analysis
questions.score_label: License plus comprehensive use guidance plus social impact analysis with mitigation
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms as above. intended_uses carries three use_category entries, each with examples and usage_notes, covering clinical machine-learning research, voice biomarker research, and methods and cohort construction. prohibited_uses carries five entries each with a stated reason, covering re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatization, IP-based restriction of downstream access, sale of the data and unapproved participant contact. discouraged_uses carries three entries with reasons: hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment and surveillance leading to discrimination. future_use_impacts carries two entries, one identifying skew-driven risks of unfair treatment and quality-of-service harms with the mitigation that users should account for the multivariate distribution, one describing the potential benefit of extending screening to low-resource settings. existing_uses records prior use in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon.
questions.quality_note: The strongest question in the record. Each of the three use-guidance slots is populated with reasoned entries rather than a single line, and every prohibition and discouragement carries its justification, which is what makes them enforceable rather than decorative. The social impact analysis is genuinely two-sided, naming both the fairness risk from cohort and site skew with a concrete mitigation and the potential benefit, and it is consistent with the fairness framing in known_biases.

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Version access, errata, updates, source derivation, parent linkages, missing data, splits and provenance representation
questions.score_label: Full provenance with entity-activity-agent relationships, processing lineage and derivation paths
questions.evidence: Entities: raw_data_sources carries three with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and access_details, from WAV recordings through REDCap exports to clinician validation forms. Activities: preprocessing_strategies gives the six-step processing chain with parameters, cleaning_strategies gives the audit protocol, and labeling_strategies gives the diagnostic labelling procedure. Agents: data_collectors names the collecting roles, labeling_strategies.annotator_demographics names the labelling clinicians, machine_annotation_tools names the nine software agents, and maintainers names the hosting and curating organizations. Derivation path: related_datasets carries derives_from to the Synapse raw-audio deposit and three is_new_version_of relations to the prior PhysioNet DOIs plus is_version_of to the concept DOI. version_access, errata and updates carry the version history. missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling. splits records that no recommended splits are provided; subsets carry is_data_split false throughout.
questions.quality_note: Goes beyond the version-history band that would cap this at 3. The lineage is traceable in both directions: from a released Parquet feature back through the named extraction library and its parameters to the WAV entity and the tablet session that produced it, and forward from each prior version to this one with the specific correction that motivated the release. Structural note: the canonical was_derived_from and parent_datasets slots are both empty, with the derivation expressed instead as a typed derives_from relation in related_datasets, so lineage is complete in content while not sitting in the slots a consumer would query first.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Known biases documented with standardized taxonomy and fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Comprehensive taxonomy-based categorization with fairness analysis, without ontology mappings
questions.evidence: known_biases carries five entries typed with enum values selection_bias, sampling_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias, each with a bias_description grounded in the collection design: recruitment from high-volume specialty clinics, non-probability sampling at limited geographic locations, English-fluency eligibility and trust-related non-participation, cohort confounding with site and tablet device, and single-labeler diagnosis without adjudication. Two entries carry mitigation_strategy and two carry affected_subsets. future_use_impacts states that models trained without accounting for the skews risk unfair treatment of groups and quality-of-service harms. known_limitations adds six typed limitation entries, and anomalies adds six data-quality observations.
questions.quality_note: Bias categorization uses the schema's controlled BiasTypeEnum values rather than free prose, the descriptions are causally specific rather than generic, and the fairness analysis in future_use_impacts uses recognizable responsible-AI harm categories. Two elements of the top band are short: no mappings to the AI Ontology or explicit CROISSANT RAI vocabulary appear anywhere, and mitigation_strategy is populated for only two of the five biases, leaving the selection, measurement and annotation biases identified but unaddressed. Scored a half band below the top on those two gaps.

strengths: Ethics and governance documentation is complete across every protection area the rubric names, and it records findings against the dataset's own interest, including that k-anonymity with k of two or more is not achieved and that the healthsheet answered 'No' to whether an impact analysis on data subjects was conducted.

Use guidance is the strongest element of the record: three intended-use categories with examples, five prohibited uses and three discouraged uses, each carrying the reason it applies, which makes the restrictions enforceable rather than decorative.

Preprocessing is documented at parameter level rather than tool level, giving window length, hop, FFT size, Mel bin count, articulatory sampling rate and pitch ranges, with a source caveat recording that v1.1 used different FFT parameters.

Provenance is a traceable chain rather than a version list, connecting released Parquet features back through named software agents and their parameters to the WAV entities and the tablet sessions that produced them, with a typed derives_from relation to the controlled-access deposit.

Source disagreements are registered rather than resolved silently. The record carries caveats for the hosting platform discrepancy, the enrollment target conflict, the recording-count figure the preferred source does not support, and inferred CRediT roles, each stating which source was preferred and why.
Access tiering is coherent across licence, distribution, governance and third-party sharing slots, so a reader can determine which tier holds the data they need and the exact steps to obtain it.

Funding is complete on both halves of the criterion, with four well-formed NIH award identifiers recorded as their sources state them and an explicit note identifying two corrupted award strings in the documentation.
weaknesses: Four keywords for a dataset covering four disease cohorts, seventeen acoustic tasks and nine derived feature families. Nothing in the keyword list would surface this record for a search on speech, dementia, Parkinson's disease, depression, chronic cough, spectrogram or machine learning.

No demographic distribution anywhere. The record names which demographic variables were collected and states that the distribution is skewed, but gives no counts or proportions by age, sex, gender, race, ethnicity or site, which is a substantive gap for a dataset whose stated purpose is demographic diversity.

The variables slot is empty although file_collections describes a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name for every released table, so no variable-level metadata is machine-readable from the datasheet itself.

No size metadata at any level. total_size_bytes, total_file_count and per-collection total_bytes are all absent, so a user cannot estimate download or storage cost for nine Parquet feature files before requesting credentialed access.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while the cohorts enroll participants with dementia, mild cognitive impairment, schizophrenia, active mood episodes and substance use disorder, which is inconsistent with the record's own cohort definitions even though special_protections states the capacity-to-consent screen.
Mitigation strategies are given for only two of five documented biases, and no bias carries a mapping to the AI Ontology or an explicit CROISSANT RAI vocabulary term.
Software version pins are uneven: b2aiprep is pinned at 3.0.0 and Whisper identified as Large, but openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, ppgs and senselab are named without versions.
parent_datasets and was_derived_from are both empty, with derivation expressed only through related_datasets, so lineage is complete in content but absent from the slots a consumer would query first.
recommendations: Expand keywords to at least eight terms drawn from content the record already carries: speech, respiratory sounds, acoustic biomarkers, machine learning, voice disorders, Parkinson's disease, dementia, depression, chronic cough.

Add a demographic breakdown to subpopulations giving counts or proportions by age band, sex, gender, race, ethnicity and collection site, or state explicitly that the release does not publish them and why.

Populate variables for at least the demographics, diagnosis and enrollment tables from the released JSON data dictionaries, or record in notes that variable-level documentation is deferred to those dictionaries.
Add total_size_bytes, or per-collection total_bytes on the features, phenotype and metadata collections, from the PhysioNet file listing.
Set at_risk_groups_included to true and use special_protections to carry the capacity-to-consent screen, so the flag matches the cohorts the record defines.
Add mitigation_strategy to the selection_bias, measurement_bias and annotation_bias entries, and add AI Ontology or CROISSANT RAI identifiers alongside the existing BiasTypeEnum values.
Pin versions for openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, ppgs and senselab in machine_annotation_tools, matching the treatment b2aiprep already receives.
Populate was_derived_from and parent_datasets with the Synapse raw-audio deposit and the prior version DOIs, keeping the related_datasets entries as the typed expression of the same relations.

Lead data_protection_impacts.impact_details with the healthsheet's own negative answer before describing the ethics review and controlled-access memorandum, so the slot is not read as a completed DPIA.
Add a note to the citation stating that RRID:SCR_007345 identifies the PhysioNet platform rather than this dataset.
